active_paradigms.idea: One-shot signed-orientation epigraph solve with free boundary vertices using scipy.optimize.minimize
active_paradigms.description: The current program uses ten differential-evolution runs followed by a local SLSQP polish, fixes all three container vertices, and locks the signs of all 165 determinants only after each DE run. Its useful principle is the barycentric (u,v) coordinate system, where every determinant equals the evaluator's normalized area exactly. Replace that runtime pipeline by one direct SLSQP call on all 11 point coordinates plus epigraph variable t, initialized from a precomputed incumbent literal. Do not force points 0, 1, and 2 to be the three container vertices; constrain every point by u>=0, v>=0, and 1-u-v>=0, since the vertex assumption is a potentially material restriction. Obtain the signed determinant pattern from the incumbent and impose sign_ijk*det_ijk(u,v)>=t for every triple, together with the triangle constraints. Supply the analytic determinant Jacobian and an analytic objective gradient for -t, exactly as the present code partly does. This directly exploits the strong local geometry discovered by the current solution while allowing the optimizer to move or release a vertex if that increases the bottleneck. Use a fixed stored incumbent and return it if the one SLSQP result is infeasible or has a smaller true unsigned minimum.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized; the formulation optimizes the evaluator's exact normalized determinant directly. It should also sharply reduce eval_time relative to ten DE searches and repeated polishing.
active_paradigms.cautions: A sign pattern is valid only locally, so this is most effective when the stored initialization is already in the desired orientation cell. Validate the returned result using unsigned determinants over all 165 triples, not merely the signed constraints. Give boundary constraints for every point, and leave a small numerical margin before Cartesian conversion to avoid violating the evaluator's 1e-6 containment tolerance.

active_paradigms.idea: Discrete threshold-feasibility construction on a triangular lattice with scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: Use a fundamentally different combinatorial certificate approach rather than searching continuous coordinates at evaluation time. Build a fixed candidate set in barycentric coordinates from a sufficiently fine triangular lattice, optionally augmented by a curated set of known good non-lattice rational locations, all of which are exactly inside u+v<=1. Choose a target normalized area slightly above the current approximately 0.793364 times benchmark, or directly test the benchmark threshold if the candidate set is rich enough. For every candidate triple whose absolute determinant is below that target, add the binary conflict inequality x_i+x_j+x_k<=2, and add the cardinality equality sum_i x_i=11. Make one scipy.optimize.milp call with integrality one and zero objective, or with a small deterministic secondary linear objective to select a reproducible feasible set. A feasible solution proves that its selected 11 points meet the threshold on the chosen candidate set, and those points can be returned directly without any continuous post-processing. This changes the difficult nonconvex area problem into a set-packing-style feasibility problem and explores orientation patterns that the current sign-locked local polish may never visit. Once an especially good discrete arrangement has been found during development, freeze its coordinates as literals in the submitted constructor for near-zero evaluation time.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly targets min_area_normalized through forbidden low-area triples, with a route to a deterministic, constant-time final returned arrangement. It trades coordinate resolution and MILP size against achievable area.
active_paradigms.cautions: The threshold must be expressed in barycentric determinant units, which are already normalized area units; do not introduce the Cartesian factor sqrt(3)/2. A full dense lattice creates O(N^3) triples, so only generate conflicts below the target and use a deliberately bounded candidate pool. If MILP reports infeasible or times out, return a validated fixed fallback rather than the fractional/undefined solution. This is a construction method; no continuous polish should be applied if maintaining the single-call design.

active_paradigms.idea: Orientation-unrestricted global basin search over all movable points with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing
active_paradigms.description: The main limitation of the current program is that its local phase cannot cross a zero-determinant orientation wall, while its global phase spends most of its work in a parameterization that permanently fixes the three corners. Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing once on all 22 unconstrained real parameters, mapping each pair deterministically into the simplex by u=sigmoid(a) and v=(1-u)*sigmoid(b). This guarantees every proposed point lies inside the equilateral triangle without penalty constraints, and unlike the current local epigraph solve the objective remains the true negative minimum of the absolute values of all 165 determinants. Set fixed bounds such as [-28,28] for each latent coordinate so the search can effectively place points on any boundary while avoiding floating-point overflow. Seed the annealer deterministically and initialize or bias its first visit around a strong stored configuration transformed into latent variables. Use a sufficiently large visit parameter and iteration budget because determinant-sign changes are precisely the transitions that must be explored. Return the best feasible mapped state tracked by the objective, not an optimizer's potentially unavailable local-search result. This is particularly useful as an offline discovery method for a new orientation basin; after discovery, hard-code the resulting coordinates for the final fast constructor.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized through the exact nonsmooth evaluator objective while removing both the fixed-corner assumption and fixed-orientation-cell restriction. Runtime is worse during discovery but becomes negligible if the discovered arrangement is frozen.
active_paradigms.cautions: Dual annealing is not competitive as a per-evaluation search if the evaluator has a tight wall-clock limit; use it to discover a literal candidate, then submit the literal. The sigmoid map only approaches exact boundaries, so use a large but safe latent bound and verify the final unsigned minimum in double precision. Point-label permutations create many equivalent states, so canonicalizing the initial literal can improve reproducibility, but do not sort dynamically in the objective because it creates artificial discontinuities.
